system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note:** The Seller's cover document labels its package "key negotiated positions" and "agreed price mechanics". Per playbook sec 0.4/6.3, nothing in it is treated as agreed, cleared or market standard. Several Seller numbers (20% cap, 18 months) happen to coincide with our conditional fallbacks; no Amelia Frost written authority exists for either, so our starting positions stand. Helpfully, the Disclosure Letter itself concedes several gaps (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, bonuses absent from funds flow) that cut against the Seller Update's assurances – we should use those admissions.

---

**SPA-N-001 – General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is only a fallback usable with prior written authority from Amelia Frost, identifying the draft – none has been given.

**SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- Recommendation: **Reject all three elements; counter at playbook levels.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the excess-only mechanic converts the basket into a permanent deductible.

**SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months post-Completion; limitation applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- Buyer wants: 24 months; no catch-all extension of the general limitation to other claim categories.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" sweep.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the sweep language would silently capture Title/Tax/IP (see N-014).

**SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright; insert standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title to the shares at 20% of what we paid for them.

**SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) – i.e. no fraud carve-out at all.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum enforceable extent.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert express fraud/wilful concealment carve-out across cl 9.3, 12 and 20.5.** This is non-negotiable and non-waivable under the playbook; a non-reliance clause purporting to cover fraud is also of doubtful enforceability and signals bad drafting intent.

**SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sched 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2]).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject [1.1]/[1.2]; require fair-disclosure standard (sufficient detail to identify nature and scope) with specific disclosures only.** Blanket data-room disclosure would neutralise the warranties entirely, and DL [1.4] already disclaims that any disclosure admits anything.

**SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete the blanket exclusion; any knowledge qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3 in full.** Combined with N-006 it would bar every claim on anything "discoverable", including constructive knowledge of our advisers – an effective zero-warranty deal.

**SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of Bluefen's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL [2] admits no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: condition precedent of effective consent AND evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery.
- Recommendation: **Reject; redraft as a hard CP requiring effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent with supporting evidence pre-Completion.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) – reasonable endeavours on a material customer consent is insufficient, and the Seller's own letter confirms it isn't in hand.

**SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL [3] confirms not repaid, no discharge included.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases/discharge at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release; require payout figure, funds-flow repayment and executed discharges (cl 9.2) as Completion deliverables.** A post-completion release could only be considered with an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval – neither exists, and the 8.1 change-of-control trigger means we'd otherwise acquire a company in default.

**SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL [5] confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- Buyer wants: bonuses plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, or expressly Seller-funded, consistent with debt-free/cash-free.
- Recommendation: **Reject silent exclusion; add a specific line item for AUD 420,000 plus on-costs (quantified) funded by the Seller / deducted from price.** "A matter for the Seller" means nothing once the Seller no longer owns the employer – the liability lands on the Company we're buying.

**SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL [4] notes cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment; AUD 180,000 shown open at DD-010 but not independently verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering non-transfer of IP, title defects, third-party claims and costs of cure, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure route; verification of payment status.
- Recommendation: **Reject as inadequate; broaden indemnity and require pre-Completion evidence of cleared payment and confirmatory assignment (or price retention pending cure).** The exposure is loss of ownership of deliverables, not merely a AUD 180,000 invoice, and the AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in either direction.

**SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sched 6). DL [6]: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification obligation undetermined.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, written updates through Completion, specific warranty/indemnity for the incident; no assumption either way on breach, harm or notification.
- Recommendation: **Reject the materiality characterisation; insert pre-Completion covenants (preserve logs, investigate, report) and a specific incident indemnity, without conceding a confirmed breach or any loss figure.** The Seller's own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary, so "not material" is an unsupported conclusion.

**SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals (3 x AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL [8] does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: assessment of timing, scope, termination rights and accrual status; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept "ordinary course" label; request DD-008/DD-011 read together and copies of renewal terms; reserve position on Debt/working-capital treatment.** The disclosure expressly refuses to characterise them, so neither side's label is yet supported.

**SPA-N-014 – Category separation**
- Seller: general regime (cap, thresholds, 18 months) applied to "all Claims"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime"; Title folded in.
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants each with their own cap/time regime; no hidden general-regime override.
- Recommendation: **Reject; add an express clause that cl 12 limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment or covenant claims.** The "unless expressly stated otherwise" wording in cl 12.3/13 is a drafting trap that would collapse every category into the weakest one.

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification**
- Seller: title to 100% evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL [10] concedes this is merely the source relied on and that Buyer verification is incomplete.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extracts, share certificates, board minutes/authority, PPSR and encumbrance searches, confirmation no options/convertibles – plus Fundamental Warranties and 100% cap.
- Recommendation: **Do not treat DD-012 as proof; require independent title/encumbrance/authority evidence as a Completion deliverable and complete our own searches.** An internal register the Seller maintains is a supplied source, not independent verification.

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: Tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP terms remain open; separate regimes to be negotiated; no assumption of unlimited liability and no resolution yet.
- Recommendation: **Reject "settled"; respond that Tax and IP are open, reserved, and to be addressed by separate Tax Indemnity and IP warranty/indemnity schedules.** A unilateral statement that terms are settled is not a negotiated outcome under playbook sec 6.3.

---

**Summary for Amelia Frost:** All 16 Seller positions are rejected or reserved. No fallback positions are triggered. The Seller Update is materially more aggressive than its own Disclosure Letter supports; our mark-up should quote DL [2], [3], [5], [6], [8] and [10] back to the Seller as grounds for the CPs and deliverables we require. Items needing principal attention before any concession: N-001 cap, N-003 time limit, N-009 Riverlark structure.
=== END ADVICE ===
